summary: Targeted 5 claims from brief.md: (1) NVIDIA's core 'SLMs match/beat larger models at 10-30x lower cost' thesis, which anchors the brief's whole optimistic narrative but is functionally single-sourced empirically despite a corroboration_count of 2; (2) the 350M-parameter model's 77.55% ToolBench pass rate beating ChatGPT-CoT/ToolLLaMA baselines, a striking single-preprint result with no independent corroboration; (3) Devstral's SWE-bench Verified SOTA trajectory, whose 3x corroboration_count is inflated since all three sources trace to the same vendor-reported figures rather than independent measurement; (4) the unresolved SWRV/CoCoS-vs-process-verification contradiction on whether self-verification scaffolds help or harm small models, targeted for reconciliation rather than a winner; and (5) the brief's own triangulated claim that RAG is a well-evidenced small-model compensator, which leans on an oracle-RAG-only, 3-model finding. Deliberately did not re-target SWE-bench Pro/SWE-EVO or the process-verification paper's own pseudo-reflection finding, since those already serve as the brief's internal counter-evidence to the optimistic narrative.
